BLOCKER: PutOptions.Immutable alone is neither enforced nor rejected: local accepts Immutable=true with Retention=0 and S3 sets no headers, so callers silently get a non-immutable object — direct violation of "enforced or explicitly rejected per provider".

S3 Put never fails when the bucket lacks object-lock (AC explicitly requires it); s.objectLock is only surfaced via Capabilities, so retention headers rely on the server rejecting them — a provider that ignores them fails open.
MAJOR: objectLock probe is one-shot best-effort: a transient GetObjectLockConfig failure pins Capabilities().ObjectLock=false for the process lifetime, and ApplyLifecycle never consults it, returning a raw provider error instead of typed datastore.ErrUnsupported.

Head's NoSuchKey→os.ErrNotExist remap is an unannounced contract change for existing callers and is not mirrored in Get; objreconcile.notFound only recognises os.ErrNotExist, so any adapter returning a store-level not-found aborts Scan instead of reporting drift.
ApplyLifecycle mutates retention then legal hold non-atomically; a failure after step one leaves partial state with no typed indication of which step succeeded.
New modules objpolicy/objreconcile rely on local `replace` directives and v0.0.0 pins; no go.work/CI wiring is shown — risk of version drift and modules silently excluded from the build/test matrix.
MINOR: Mint checks capability before method/TTL, so deny-reason ordering leaks which gate tripped; only denials are logged — no audit record of successful mint (no request/tenant id either).
tenantPrefix is a plain parameter; the comment claims it comes from authenticated context but nothing enforces or derives it from ctx.
Scan's Actual is counted from the raw List slice while comparisons use the deduped map (duplicate keys skew counts); size is taken from List despite the doc saying Head is authoritative.
ObjectLifecycle calls GetBucketVersioning on every invocation — an extra round trip per object that should be cached from the constructor probe.
Scan aborts on the first transient Head error, discarding all already-detected drift rather than returning a partial report plus error.
Missing tests for the Head-failure fail-closed path, prefix normalization, and JSON determinism of Report.
NIT: cleanPath's `strings.Contains(c, "..")` is unreachable after path.Clean, giving false confidence in the guard.
New modules hardcode `go 1.21`; confirm against the repo toolchain/go.work version.
success path of Mint and reconcile's clean runs are silent — a single DEBUG/INFO line would help operational triage.
SUMMARY: Solid shape overall: optional capability + typed ErrUnsupported, a single signed-URL privilege boundary, and a read-only deterministic reconcile report are the right primitives.

Top risks: fail-open handling of PutOptions.Immutable and of object-lock-less buckets violates explicit ACs; the one-shot objectLock probe and inconsistent not-found typing undermine the fail-closed guarantees across providers.
Before merge: enforce/reject Immutable everywhere, fail fast on missing object-lock, unify not-found semantics, and confirm the new modules are wired into workspace/CI.
